Subject: Residency and deletion guarantees for Private deployment

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. AtlasEdge is evaluating Redwood Private for a subset of our customer workloads that must remain in-region (US-only) and where the customer retains exclusive control of the storage layer. Legal/security has a short list of must-haves before we proceed: 

- Confirmation that customer-controlled storage (S3-like object store or on-prem NFS) can be used for model inputs/outputs and logs, with Redwood never copying data to other accounts/regions without explicit config.
- Support for Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) via AWS KMS or HSM such that Redwood cannot decrypt data without a customer key.
- A deletion workflow: ability for AtlasEdge to trigger a full tenant wipe (data + KV caches + snapshots) and a timeline for completion.
- Evidence of deletion: audit logs and a signed attestation we can include in our compliance package.
- Any residual backups / retained artifacts and their default retention periods; how to shorten them if required.

Could you please run these by your security team and provide a short Q&A we can share with our lawyers? Ideally something we can attach to the SOW.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Baird

Subject: RE: Residency and deletion guarantees for Private deployment — Q&A and artifacts

Hi Evelyn — thanks for the prompt. Below is a concise Q&A and the evidence options AtlasEdge can request for inclusion in an SOW or security addendum. I kept answers short for legal; happy to expand any item.

Q1: Can AtlasEdge use customer-controlled storage so Redwood never copies data to other regions/accounts?
A1: Yes. Redwood Private supports two deployment modes: customer-managed object stores (S3-compatible) mounted into the runtime and on-prem object/NAS. When configured, model inputs/outputs, logs, and persistent artifacts are written only to the customer-controlled endpoint. By default, Redwood does not replicate tenant data across regions unless explicit cross-region replication is enabled in your config.

Q2: BYOK / KMS / HSM support — does Redwood have access to plaintext?
A2: We support BYOK via AWS KMS and external HSMs. Customers can provision keys that are used to encrypt persistent stores and snapshots. Redwood processes running in your VPC can be configured to request decryption tokens via a short-lived, customer-controlled role; Redwood services do not retain long-term access to your key material. If AtlasEdge requires cryptographic separation (zero-knowledge), we can scope the deployment so that critical decryption operations only occur in customer-owned hosts.

Q3: How is a tenant wipe initiated and what is the expected completion timeline?
A3: Tenant wipe can be initiated by: (a) AtlasEdge via API/console (DeleteTenant endpoint + confirmation), (b) Redwood support acting on an approved deletion ticket, or (c) automated teardown following contract termination. The wipe procedure removes active objects, KV caches, snapshots, and derived indexes. Typical completion: 48–168 hours (2–7 days) depending on dataset size and snapshotting. SOW can specify target windows (we frequently commit to 7–30 day windows; 30 days is common for enterprise SLA).

Q4: What about backups, replication, and retained artifacts?
A4: Backups and snapshots are configurable. Default backup retention is 90 days for the managed snapshot cadence, but this can be reduced to meet tighter requirements. When a wipe is requested, we remove primary objects and coordinate the purge of snapshots and backups in your configured retention window; we document which artifacts were deleted and when.

Q5: Evidence & attestation options?
A5: Options we can provide: (1) Deletion event log (signed timestamped record with object counts and digests), (2) Exportable audit trail (CloudTrail-style events for all deletion API calls), (3) Signed attestation letter from Redwood security describing actions taken and referencing secure audit exports, (4) Optional live demonstration / PoC where AtlasEdge triggers a wipe in a test tenant and we jointly validate artifact removal.

Q6: Are there residual metadata or index artifacts that persist outside customer storage?
A6: Metadata required for operation (service records, routing pointers) may remain in the Redwood control plane only when explicitly permitted. For Private deployments with strict data minimization, we support a Local Control Plane option where control metadata resides in your VPC. If you require zero metadata retention in Redwood-hosted control plane, we will need to adopt the private control plane deployment and document the scope in the SOW.

Q7: Compliance reports (SOC 2 / attestation)?
A7: Redwood provides SOC 2 Type II reports. For AtlasEdge-specific attestations we offer a residency attestation template (attached) that we can sign post-wipe and include supplemental audit exports.

Next steps we recommend:
- Decide whether you prefer customer-managed object store or full on-prem storage (we can produce configuration steps for both).
- If BYOK + zero-knowledge is required, confirm whether decryption should be constrained to customer-owned hosts.
- Agree deletion SLA window (we can contractually commit to 7 days for most tenants; exceptions for very large snapshots can be handled case-by-case).
- Schedule a PoC run in a test tenant so legal sees the live deletion evidence.

I've attached the residency attestation template and a concise delete-playbook that maps API calls to expected audit records. If you want tightened language for the SOW, we can provide a suggested clause.

Regards,
Marissa Cole

Tom/Evelyn — all good. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Attestation fields: we include object path/prefix, object count, SHA256 digest summary (per-archive), deletion timestamp (ISO8601), initiating principal (email/role), tenant id, and a signed Redwood security signature block (PGP signature or signed PDF). We can provide raw audit exports as gzipped JSON for your auditors.
- Timeline: we can run a PoC in a test tenant and demonstrate full wipe within 48 hours for the sample dataset size you indicated; formal attestation can be produced within 3 business days post-wipe. For production tenants we will contractually commit to a 7-day deletion SLA by default; if you require 3-day we can scope that in the SOW with an availability/throughput commitment.

Proposed PoC slot: Mon 10/15 09:00 PT — Redwood will prepare a test tenant, AtlasEdge will seed a small dataset, AtlasEdge triggers a DeleteTenant call, Redwood demonstrates deletion and provides the signed attestation. Please confirm and we'll send a calendar invite + pre-PoC checklist.
